chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Abd al-Samin, who narrated that he raised it to the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) was delivering a sermon to the people while saying, 'Ask me before you lose me! By Allah, you will not ask me about anything that has passed or anything that will occur, except that I will inform you of it.' He said, 'So Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas stood up to him and said, 'O Commander of the Believers! Inform me, how many hairs are on my head and in my beard?' He said to him, 'By Allah, you have asked me about a matter my beloved, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), informed me of: that you would ask me about it. And there is not a single hair on your head or in your beard except that a devil is seated at its root. And there is a lamb in your house that will kill my son, Husayn.' (Asbagh added), 'And Umar was playing at that time in front of his father.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the number of hairs on Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas's head?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights Imam Ali’s (a.s.) claim to comprehensive knowledge (*'Ilm al-Ghayb*) of both the past and future, a key theological point in Shia scholarship. The specific mention of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and the prophetic sign of a lamb killing Husayn (a.s.) connects the event to the broader narrative of the Ahl al-Bayt's martyrdom, while the detail of Umar 'drudging' (crawling or moving hurriedly) adds historical texture to the scene. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the divine foreknowledge attributed to the Imams regarding their own fate.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 12. My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdil Jabbār, from ‘Abdil Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, from Ja’far ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥukaym, from ‘Abd Al-Samīn, who narrated that:

(One day) while the Commander of the Believers (a.s.) was delivering a sermon to the people he said, “Ask me before you lose me! I swear to Allāh that I will answer (your questions about) anything you might ask that has happened in the past or will happen in the future.” So Sa’d ibn Abī Waqqās got up and asked, “O Commander of the Believers! Tell me about the number of hairs that I have on my head and in my beard?” The Commander of the Believers (a.s.) replied, “I swear to Allāh that my love, the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.), informed me that you would be asking me this question. There is a Shayťān rooted in every strand of hair on your head and in your beard and there is a baby sheep in your house who will kill my son, Ḥusain (a.s.).” (‘Abd Al-Samīn/Asbagh added), “’Umar ibn Sa’d (the killer of Imam Ḥusain (a.s.)) was a child then and he was playing in front of his father (Sa’d ibn Abī Waqqās).”
